client_brief:
NIGHTFORM: Low Beam release cut and vertical

Project overview
NIGHTFORM is a self released electronic project built on mood: late, atmospheric, cinematic tracks that sound like driving at night. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Low Beam release cut and vertical and Low Beam release stills, six beats.

What we will provide
source_video_files/ (1 measured short file); motion_source_metadata.json; source_video_files/ (1 measured short file); nightform_shotlist.md; nightform_wordmark.png (1400 x 400, flat); nightform_card_2024.pdf; nightform_captions.txt; nightform_formats.csv. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Low Beam release cut and vertical: A deliberate 4-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 1 supplied short clip using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. 
- Low Beam release stills, six beats: Six frames pulled from the take and brought to one night target: one black point, one warmth, one grain, one sense of how much roadway stays legible, all at or below the take's native frame dimensions. 

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.

Source-media note
The supplied package contains 1 video file totaling 5.042 seconds, 0 with embedded audio, and 0 separate audio files. These measured values are the production limits.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$2,500-$6,500 fixed; target delivery 2 to 4 weeks; one direction checkpoint and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Anchor: the Freelancer.com post quoted in the ledger grounding_note, from a short form vertical video creator looking for a freelance editor to turn raw night footage into a post ready package with, in the poster's own words, on brand colour, a scroll stopping cover, and captions for the vertical short video feeds. The real post named a person, a handle and the editing app; all three are laundered to the coined fictional artist NIGHTFORM, with platform names replaced by the generic vertical short video feeds. The real post is thin because the poster described only the last mile. The fuller commission that client genuinely needed is the one written here: the still imagery for the release comes out of the same take as the video, so the frames and the cut have to be one piece of art direction rather than two jobs; the sleeve card that ships with the physical editions exists only as the printer's PDF from the previous release and has to be reprinted across six formats; and the wordmark survives only as a flat image. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that fuller job honest: a press PDF can be reverse engineered into a live merge template headlessly, HTML authoring returns a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes, and an ink level trace recovers a real mark rather than inventing one.

price_band_and_audience: Self released independent electronic single, no label, streaming first listeners aged roughly 19 to 34, physical editions at 12 to 28 dollars through independent record shops. The band is load bearing: at this level the release is bought on mood and on the sense that one person made it, so the look has to be dark, grainy, cinematic and slightly rough. The identical assets graded bright, clean, saturated and evenly lit would read as a car commercial or a stock library reel, and on an electronic release that misfile is fatal in a way no technical gate catches. Push the other way into total blackness and unreadable type and the record disappears in a feed that is watched at arm's length on a phone in daylight. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 1,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Self released independent electronic music. Streaming first, with physical vinyl and cassette editions through independent record shops.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A solo project running since 2020 in Portland, Oregon. One artist who writes, produces and releases everything without a label.
brand_identity.about: NIGHTFORM is a self released electronic project built on mood: late, atmospheric, cinematic tracks that sound like driving at night. The next single, Low Beam, is bought on feeling and on the sense that one person made the whole thing, so every visual has to carry the same nocturnal weight as the music.
brand_identity.audience: Streaming listeners roughly nineteen to thirty four who follow the mood. Physical buyers pay twelve to twenty eight dollars for vinyl and cassette through independent shops.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Independent, no label, priced as a self released record. The look has to be dark, grainy and slightly rough, never bright, clean and commercial, which would read as a car advert or a stock reel. Total blackness is the other failure: the road still has to be legible on a phone in daylight.
brand_identity.typography: A clean geometric or grotesque sans set tight and quiet, letting the imagery carry the mood. Captions and the artist name stay legible over dark moving frames at arm's length. No script, no ornament, no filmic distress on the letterforms.
brand_identity.voice: Spare and evocative, closer to a liner note than a sales line. Example line the brand would write: "Low Beam. Recorded from the passenger seat, north of the city, around eleven at night."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The wordmark survives only as a flat exported picture: separated white capitals on a solid black square, from a source file no one still has. It has to be recovered as usable artwork. The previous release's sleeve card exists only as the printer's press PDF, and the whole visual identity for this single comes out of one forty five second night take.
brand_identity.values: One person, one mood, made without a label. The artist changes the words up to the drop date and cannot re commission, so anything text bearing has to stay editable.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_shotlist.md
assets_supplied.kind: The artist's own notes on the take, seven beats described by feel with rough minute markings rather than timecode.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The bits I keep coming back to. Roughly where they are."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One of the seven beats described is not in this take at all: it is remembered from a different night's footage that was never supplied, and only looking at the frames rather than the notes settles which six actually exist.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_wordmark.png (1400 x 400, flat)
assets_supplied.kind: The artist's wordmark as a flat picture: separated capital letterforms in white on a solid black square, exported years ago from a file nobody still has.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only wordmark I have. It is just a picture of it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The letterforms are disjoint, so a subject led knockout keeps two of them and drops the rest while reporting success, and a trace comes back with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle at path zero. That rectangle is black here, so it is invisible against a night frame and only reveals itself when the mark lands on the sleeve card's pale board.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_card_2024.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's press PDF of the previous release's sleeve card: a small format card with a title line, a catalogue number, a format line and a date, set in one column over a pale board with the wordmark at the head.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the printer has. Same card, new record."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The four printed lines are one continuous text flow rather than four separate blocks, so the conversion exposes nothing like the per line frame structure the printed card implies. The readout that a field map would be computed from also omits one run while keeping its line break, so every offset past that point is short and the validator still passes the map as valid.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_captions.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Twelve caption cues for the overlay set, plus the artist name line and the release line, with per cue positions numbered against the full take.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The words. They will change, which is why I need to be able to edit them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The cue positions are numbered against the whole forty five seconds, so cues sitting in passages a shortened cut does not contain no longer have anywhere to land, and one cue is a two line lyric roughly three times the length of every other.

assets_supplied.name: nightform_formats.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Six rows, one per format: title line, catalogue number, format, release date, and a shop or press flag.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six cards I need. One row each."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The vinyl row carries a release date two weeks later than the other five because the pressing runs late, which the brief's single drop date does not admit.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which visible beats in the measured short clips actually cut together without a continuity jump, duplicate action, or missing subject.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Filenames and source duration do not establish visual continuity. The first assembled proof is the earliest reliable evidence.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Replace or reorder source ranges, shorten the piece, and rebuild the EDL around the strongest continuous action.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A technically valid render feels accidental or implies an action that the source never completes.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the approved horizontal composition survives the required vertical or square reframe with the subject and essential interface or product detail still visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The crop depends on the actual chosen ranges and subject position inside each rendered frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Choose a different source range for the platform version or use fit instead of fill and revise the surrounding design treatment.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The platform export is correctly sized but loses the person, product, or interface that gives the shot meaning.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the silent final piece still communicates clearly without implying dialogue, ambience, or music that was never supplied.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: This can be judged only on the final rendered sequence, not from a successful operation response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Strengthen visual sequencing or approved on-screen copy without fabricating a soundtrack.
